2) Marketplace: We prefer to purchase via our cloud marketplace (AWS Marketplace) if possible because of our internal chargeback and approval flow. If Redwood can list pricing and an AMI/marketplace offering, procurement will be faster.

3) Attached is FintechX's standard PO template and our procurement checklist. For anything over $50k/year, legal will need to engage for indemnity/DPAs.

I'm copying procurement (procurement@fintechx.com) so they can confirm timelines.

Hi all — adding a short technical note to help with the commercial matrix: 

- Hosted (Redwood API): fastest to start, billed per-token / per-embedding. No infra commitments. Good for pilot and for teams that want minimal ops. Typical pilot SKU: 10k reqs/month, pay-as-you-go.

- Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity with monthly commit. Predictable throughput and dedicated tenancy. Pricing is a monthly commit (e.g., 3 x V100-equivalent slots) and we provide SLA and capacity guarantees. Better for high-throughput payment flows or low-latency needs.

- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated workloads requiring customer-managed network and KMS/HSM. Licensing + deployment fee + ongoing ops support; usually procured via enterprise contract and longer lead time.

Notes re Marketplace: if you purchase via AWS Marketplace, billing flows through AWS (we provide an AMI/marketplace listing). There can be invoicing and revenue-share implications; pricing sometimes reflects marketplace fees.

I've attached a brief snippet of SKU line items we recommend for the PO. Happy to jump on the call Fri to walk through.

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
